details: The blind-write retained `Timer` irqmode support even though current-tree rnull supports only `None` and `Soft`.
The blind-write root `features` output advertised `power`, while current-tree rnull advertises only `blocksize,size,rotational,irqmode`.
Both implementations model a configfs root that creates child devices and gate configuration changes while powered on.
Blind-write uses split `config` and `live` mutexes plus explicit `drop_item` power-off.
Current-tree rnull uses one mutex containing powered state and `disk: Option<GenDisk<_>>`.
For `None` and `Soft` irq modes, the blind-write request completion strategy matches the official ownership direction: queue request, optionally remote complete, and end the request exactly once.
Queue data is foreign-owned at disk build time and reclaimed on `GenDisk` drop in the blind-write abstraction, so ownership is paired.
The extra `Timer` path is a scope expansion, not evidence that the official subset became less sound.

aligned_items: Driver layer stays zero unsafe in both the blind-write and current-tree reference.
Both implementations put the live block object under configfs child ownership.
Both implementations reject config changes while powered on.
Both implementations use blk-mq queue data to carry irq-mode choice.
misaligned_items: Blind-write adds `Timer` irqmode support beyond current-tree rnull.
Blind-write root `features` string includes `power` while current-tree rnull does not.
Blind-write build integration switches C versus Rust in the same DUT slot, while current-tree rnull is a standalone module `rnull_mod`.
old_tree_constraints: The true pre-rnull baseline at `3253aba3408aa4eb2e4e09365eede3e63ef7536b` predates the current-tree rotational configfs attribute, so the rerun mixes a historical baseline with a later frozen compare scope.
Historical-tree compilation on host rustc 1.82 required compatibility fixes in `rust/kernel/alloc/box_ext.rs` and `scripts/Makefile.build` that do not change the driver semantics.
workflow_gaps: The pattern library did not yet contain a configfs child plus powered block-mq registration pattern.
The existing rule set did not call out the need to audit both `drop_item` and final release for configfs children that own registered objects.
